conditions.label: Acute ischemic stroke, right frontal lobe

reports.text: CT HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST. Indication: new left leg weakness. Technique: axial noncontrast images of the head. Findings: Small area of hypodensity in the right frontal lobe. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. Basal cisterns patent. Calvarium intact.
reports.conclusion: Small right frontal hypodensity, compatible with acute ischemic infarct in this clinical setting. No hemorrhage.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD (received from a regional hospital; date of service 5/25/2025)

CC: left foot dragging

HPI: 68-year-old man brought in by his wife, who saw him catching the toes of his left foot as he walked this afternoon. He has no pain anywhere. Describes the left leg as hard to pick up. No headache, no speech trouble, no arm symptoms. No previous stroke or TIA.

PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia. PSH: cataract surgery (2021).
Home meds: lisinopril, atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father with ischemic stroke at 74; mother hypertensive; brother with CAD.
Social: retired accountant. Ex-smoker, 35 pack-years, quit 2017. Alcohol once or twice monthly.

Exam: Awake, alert, oriented x3. CN II-XII intact. Strength 5/5 bilateral upper extremities and right lower extremity; left lower extremity 3/5 with mildly increased tone. Sensation intact throughout. Normal finger-to-nose bilaterally; upper-extremity reflexes normal.

CT head noncontrast: small right frontal hypodensity, no hemorrhage.
Labs: CBC, BMP and INR unremarkable.

Impression: acute ischemic stroke, right frontal lobe, with left leg weakness.
Disposition: admitted to the hospital for stroke care.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY (regional hospital)
Admitted 5/25/2025, discharged 5/27/2025.

Principal diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, right frontal lobe.
Other: hypertension, hyperlipidemia.

Course: Presented with left leg weakness noticed by his wife. Noncontrast CT head showed a small right frontal hypodensity without hemorrhage. Monitored on the medical floor with neuro checks. The left leg weakness improved steadily over two days; by discharge he was walking the hallway with physical therapy, still catching the left foot occasionally. Fasting lipids and A1c were in range on his current regimen.

Discharge medications (unchanged):
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: home with his wife. Outpatient physical therapy for the left leg. Follow up with his PCP within 1 to 2 weeks and with neurology clinic in about 6 months. Return for any new weakness, numbness, speech or vision change.

documents.title: Transitional Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with pt and wife, home since yesterday afternoon after a 2-day stay for a right frontal stroke. ED and discharge records in the chart. He says the leg is "better every day" but he still scuffs the left toe when tired. No new symptoms. Has both meds at home, no changes made by the hospital. Using a railing on the stairs. Reviewed stroke warning signs and calling 911. Post-discharge visit booked Mon 6/2 with PCP. Wife will drive.

orders.reason: Left leg weakness after right frontal stroke

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with his wife one week after a right frontal ischemic stroke (admitted 5/25 to 5/27 at a regional hospital; ED record and discharge summary reviewed).

He feels the left leg is close to normal on short walks but tires and drags on longer ones. No new weakness, numbness, slurred speech or visual symptoms since discharge. No falls. Thinking feels clear to him and to his wife. Taking lisinopril and atorvastatin as before.

Exam: BP as recorded. Alert, conversant, speech normal. Left hip flexion and ankle dorsiflexion a little weaker than the right; otherwise strength full. Gait: slight left foot slap at speed, no assistive device. Heart regular, no carotid bruits.

A/P
- Acute ischemic stroke, right frontal, with residual left leg weakness: outpatient PT referral placed as the hospital advised. Neurology clinic follow-up around November.
- HTN: continue lisinopril 20.
- HLD: continue atorvastatin 40.
- Not to drive until cleared after therapy; wife driving for now.
Recheck at the fall wellness visit, sooner if needed.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL THERAPY, INITIAL EVALUATION (date of service 6/9/2025)
Referral: PCP, left lower extremity weakness after right frontal ischemic stroke 5/25/2025.

Subjective: wants to get back to his morning walks without his foot catching. No falls.
Objective: Left hip flexion and ankle dorsiflexion weak compared with the right. Gait with intermittent left foot drag, more with fatigue and on turns. Independent indoors without a device. Transfers independent.
Assessment: gait deviation from left leg weakness, good potential.
Plan: twice weekly for 8 weeks; strengthening, gait training, balance; home exercise program.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body: PT DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 15 visits from 6/9 to 8/12/2025. Gait improved; walks community distances without a device and without foot drag on level ground. Balance improved. Discharged to a home exercise program, which he does daily per report. No device recommended. Thank you.

documents.title: Call From Daughter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Daughter called (pt gave verbal OK on the line). She has been staying with her parents this week and says over the last several days her dad has been forgetting things, losing track of what he's doing and can't seem to organize his day, which is not like him at all. He tells me he feels a bit weaker on the left again. Per daughter no facial droop, no slurred speech, no new trouble walking, no fall. He has his 6-month neurology appointment Monday 11/17. Advised keeping that appointment and having her go with him. Any new weakness, speech change, facial asymmetry or worsening confusion before then: call 911. Will see him here after neurology.

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY CLINIC (regional hospital stroke clinic), visit 11/17/2025

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Rousseau, 68, for his planned follow-up six months after his right frontal ischemic stroke. His daughter came with him and supplied most of the history. Across the past week she has seen an abrupt change in him: he forgets recent conversations, drifts off task, and cannot lay out his day the way he always has; she stresses he has been a meticulous planner his whole life. He himself mentions only that the left side feels mildly weak.

Background: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, the May stroke. Cataract surgery 2021. Medications lisinopril and atorvastatin. NKDA. Father had an ischemic stroke at 74, mother hypertension, brother coronary disease. Former smoker (35 pack-years, stopped 2017), rare alcohol, retired accountant.

Examination: alert, though flat and apathetic in manner. Language fluent without aphasia. Cranial nerves normal. Mild drift of the left arm and leg. Sensation normal.

Noncontrast head CT today: small, well-circumscribed right frontal hypodensity at the site of the known infarct, no new lesion.

Impression: vascular dementia following the right frontal infarct, with predominantly executive and attention problems and apathy.

Recommendations: continue blood pressure and cholesterol treatment as you are. Please check vitamin B12 and TSH if not recent. A baseline cognitive screen in your office would be useful. I advised that he not drive. Family to help with finances and medications. I will see him again in about six months.

Sincerely,
Stroke neurology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Cognition Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife and daughter after his 11/17 neurology visit (letter reviewed). Neurology's impression is vascular dementia after the May right frontal stroke.

Family: since mid-November he has been less himself. Misplaces things, loses the thread of what he started, needs prompting to get going in the morning. No hallucinations, no wandering, no getting lost in familiar places. Sleep and appetite fine. Mood: he says "fine" and doesn't seem sad, more indifferent. He is not driving. Daughter has taken over the bills and checkbook with his agreement. Wife fills his pill box on Sundays.

MoCA 22/30. Lost points on trails, clock, delayed recall and serial 7s; oriented fully.
Exam: BP as recorded. Flat affect, cooperative, speech fluent. Mild left drift. Gait steady.

A/P
1. Vascular dementia: MoCA 22 today as baseline. B12 and TSH drawn per neurology. Reviewed what to expect, home safety, keeping a daily routine and his walks. No medication for this now. Family to call with any sudden change.
2. Ischemic stroke, right frontal: on lisinopril and atorvastatin as before.
3. HTN: a little high today, usually at goal; recheck in March before any change. 4. HLD: continue atorvastatin 40.
No driving, agreed by all. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: B12 and thyroid results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Dennis (and family), the vitamin B12 came back at 486 and the thyroid test at 2.1. Both normal, so neither is contributing to the memory changes. No new treatment needed. See you in March.
